'''Cyril Despres''' (born 24 January 1974)<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.redbull.com/cs/Satellite/en_INT/Profile/CyrilDespres--DakarRallyDrivers--RedBull-021242746278373 |title=Cyril Despres -- Motor Sports Profiles |publisher=[[Red Bull]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120404040838/https://www.redbull.com/cs/Satellite/en_INT/Profile/CyrilDespres--DakarRallyDrivers--RedBull-021242746278373 |archive-date=4 April 2012 |access-date=31 July 2021}}</ref> is a French [[rally racing|rally racer]] and resident of [[Andorra]].<ref>[http://www.wxec.info/rider-pages/cyril-despres.html World Xtreme Enduro Championship – Cyril Despres] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110717083923/http://www.wxec.info/rider-pages/cyril-despres.html |date=2011-07-17 }}</ref> He won the [[Dakar Rally]] five times, in [[2005 Dakar Rally|2005]], [[2007 Dakar Rally|2007]], [[2010 Dakar Rally|2010]], [[2012 Dakar Rally|2012]] and [[2013 Dakar Rally|2013]],<ref>[http://www.dakar.com/dakar/2011/us/rider/002.html Rider sheet – Cyril DESPRES] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110105141910/http://www.dakar.com/dakar/2011/us/rider/002.html |date=2011-01-05 }}</ref> riding a [[KTM]] motorcycle. He also won the [[Red Bull Romaniacs Hard Enduro Rallye|Red Bull Romaniacs]], an [[enduro]] event, three times, in 2004, 2005 and 2007, and the [[Erzberg Rodeo]] in 2002 and 2003.<ref>[http://www.motocorse.com/news/enduro_eng/15142_Cyril_Despres_the_07_RB_Romaniacs_Rally_and_the_brand_new_2008_model_KTM_300_EXC-E.php Cyril Despres, the 07 RB Romaniacs Rally and the brand new 2008 model KTM 300 EXC-E]</ref> In the 2018 season he is one of the official drivers of the [[Team Peugeot Total]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.redbull.com/int-en/projects/team-peugeot-total/teams|title=Team Peugeot Total - The team|publisher=redbull.com|accessdate=21 January 2018}}</ref>

==Career==
On 10 January 2012, at the [[2012 Dakar Rally]], Portuguese pilot [[Paulo Gonçalves (motorcyclist)|Paulo Gonçalves]] pulled Despres out of the mud but Cyril did not return the favour. Out of seven riders, all but the Spaniard [[Marc Coma]] got stuck; the organisers therefore changed the course. At the end of the stage, the time lost was credited to Despres. Goncalves received a penalty of six hours for receiving external help. Coma was not credited the time he lost by going around the mudhole.<ref>[http://www.redbull.com/cs/Satellite/en_INT/Article/Cyril-Despres%E2%80%99s-Blog-Dakar-Rally-Muddy-mayhem-021243146826509 Cyril Despres’s Blog: Dakar Rally | Muddy mayhem], Cyril Despres, 2012-01-10.</ref><ref>[http://www.foxsports.com.au/motor-sports/dakar/cyril-despres-gives-marco-coma-a-commanding-lead-with-mistake-on-stage-eight-of-the-dakar-rally/story-fn5k5ou0-1226240395302 Cyril Despres gives Marc Coma a commanding lead with mistake on stage eight of the Dakar Rally], 2012-01-10, foxsports australia.</ref><ref>[http://dailypicksandflicks.com/2012/01/12/2012-dakar-rally-fair-play-abandoned-in-the-mud-video/ 2012 Dakar Rally: Fair Play Abandoned in the Mud (Video)] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140111084616/http://dailypicksandflicks.com/2012/01/12/2012-dakar-rally-fair-play-abandoned-in-the-mud-video/ |date=2014-01-11 }}, dave on dailypicsandflics with the video of Despres deserting Goncalves, 2012-01-10.</ref><ref>[http://www.racing.speedbrain.de/press/rally-reports-english/71-dakar-2012-stage-11 Barreda in the top five again] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140111085225/http://www.racing.speedbrain.de/press/rally-reports-english/71-dakar-2012-stage-11 |date=2014-01-11 }}, Goncalves speedbrain Team site, 2012-01-10.</ref><ref>[http://www.cyclenews.com/194/13367/Racing-Article/Goncalves-Penalized-6-Hours-In-Dakar.aspx Goncalves Penalized 6 Hours In Dakar] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140111084742/http://www.cyclenews.com/194/13367/Racing-Article/Goncalves-Penalized-6-Hours-In-Dakar.aspx |date=2014-01-11 }}, 2012-01-12.</ref>

After a closely fought battle with his KTM teammate, Spaniard [[Marc Coma]] for the victory, Despres got back into the lead on the penultimate stage (Stage 13) thanks to a mechanical failure on Coma's bike. Despres managed to maintain the lead until the end of the rally. Thus, Despres gained his fourth overall victory on the Dakar Rally, equaling former [[Honda]] and [[Cagiva]] rider, Italian [[Edi Orioli]]'s performance.

A new chapter began in his Dakar career in [[2015 Dakar Rally|2015]] when he joined the Peugeot team as a driver alongside [[Carlos Sainz Sr.|Carlos Sainz]] and [[Stéphane Peterhansel]], who previously switched from the motorbike to car category with great success. His co-driver was Gilles Picard, and they finished 34th. In 2016, Despres came in seventh overall; his co-driver was David Castera.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.dakar.com/dakar/2016/us/stage-1400/rankings/overall-cars.html#ancre|title=General ranking stage 13 car page :Dakar|last=Organisation|first=A.S.O. - Amaury Sport|access-date=2016-07-30}}</ref>

In July 2016, Despres and Castera won the cars' category at the [[Silk Way Rally]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.silkwayrally.com/rally2016/news/the-silk-way-flame/|title=The Silk Way Flame|website=www.silkwayrally.com|access-date=2016-07-30|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160730190121/http://www.silkwayrally.com/rally2016/news/the-silk-way-flame/|archive-date=2016-07-30|url-status=dead}}</ref> Despres and his partner repeated their success in the next year.<ref>[http://www.silkwayrally.com/en/news/s.14-despres-and-sotnikov-score-doubles-at-xi%E2%80%99an.html S.14 Despres and Sotnikov score doubles at Xi’an]</ref>
